title: Alcohol & Drunkenness
summary: Drunkenness is forbidden; Christian liberty is governed by wisdom and love.
context: Paul describes a Spirit-filled community through worship, thanksgiving, and mutual submission in 5:19–21.
distinction: Reject drunkenness and let wisdom and love govern decisions about drinking (Romans 14:21).

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Ephesians 5
insights.quote: he forbids excessive and immoderate drinking of every description

title: Marriage
summary: Marriage calls for covenant faithfulness and sacrificial love.
context: Jesus answers a question about divorce by bringing his hearers back to the creation of husband and wife in Genesis 2.
distinction: Treat marriage as a covenant of lifelong fidelity and practice the self-giving love described in Ephesians 5:25.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Matthew 19
insights.quote: that every man should sacredly observe the promise which he has given

title: Anxiety
summary: Bring worries to God in prayer and trust his care.
context: Paul connects prayer and thanksgiving to the nearness of the Lord and the peace that guards believers.
distinction: Bring concrete needs to God. The passage encourages anxious people to pray and receive care.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Philippians 4
insights.quote: There are many things that saints are to be careful for

title: Forgiveness
summary: Christians are called to forgive as they have been forgiven.
context: Paul contrasts destructive speech and bitterness with the practices of a community renewed in Christ.
distinction: God’s forgiveness grounds ours. Forgiving someone can coexist with accountability and appropriate boundaries.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Ephesians 4
insights.quote: they should forgive, and should pray to God for one another

title: Salvation
summary: Salvation is by grace through faith, not earned by works.
context: Paul moves from spiritual death to God making sinners alive with Christ, then identifies the purpose of that grace.
distinction: Receive salvation by faith as God’s gift. Good works are its intended fruit.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Ephesians 2
insights.quote: salvation is not a reward or recompense, but unmixed grace

title: Money & Wealth
summary: Wealth is not ultimate security; practice generosity and contentment.
context: Paul corrects teachers who see godliness as a route to financial gain and reminds Timothy of human mortality.
distinction: Practice contentment and heed Paul’s call for the wealthy to be generous in verses 17–19.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · 1 Timothy 6
insights.quote: it is an immoderate insatiable desire after it

title: Suffering
summary: Believers can trust God amid suffering without denying its pain.
context: The chain from suffering to hope follows Paul’s assurance of peace with God through justification.
distinction: Endurance grows under pressure, and hope rests in God’s love poured out by the Spirit.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Romans 5
insights.quote: all the sorrows we endure contribute to our salvation and final good

title: Judgment
summary: Avoid hypocritical judgment while practicing righteous discernment.
context: Jesus uses the plank and speck to expose the hypocrisy of a critic who ignores his own fault.
distinction: Start with self-examination and offer correction humbly, as Galatians 6:1 also teaches.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Matthew 7
insights.quote: rash judgment, interpreting men's words and deeds to the worst sense

title: Philippians 4:13
summary: Christ strengthens Paul to endure changing circumstances, not to achieve every ambition.
context: Paul is thanking the Philippians for their support. The preceding verse names hunger and plenty as circumstances he has learned to face.
distinction: Christ supplies strength for contentment in need and abundance. Paul is describing endurance through both circumstances.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Philippians 4
insights.quote: how to behave himself in adversity and prosperity

title: Matthew 7:1
summary: Jesus condemns hypocritical judgment, not every moral assessment.
context: The warning about judgment leads to a picture of a man removing his own plank so he can see clearly to help his brother.
distinction: Jesus requires honest self-judgment and mercy in correction. The rest of the chapter still calls for discernment.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Matthew 7
insights.quote: always begins with subjecting himself to examination, and preserves a proper medium and order in his judgments

title: Jeremiah 29:11
summary: God promises a future to the exiled community, not immediate individual prosperity.
context: Jeremiah writes to Judean exiles. They must settle in Babylon and seek its welfare during a long exile before God brings his people back.
distinction: Read the promise as God’s pledge to his exiled people. It gives grounds for hope during a long wait.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Jeremiah 29
insights.quote: The purposes and resolutions of his heart concerning their welfare, particularly the restoration of them to their own land

title: Matthew 18:20
summary: Jesus promises his presence in the context of communal accountability and prayer.
context: The two or three appear in a section about confronting sin, bringing witnesses, and involving the church.
distinction: Jesus assures disciples of his presence as they carry out this difficult work together in his name.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Matthew 18
insights.quote: therefore no reason to doubt that those who give themselves up to his direction will derive most desirable advantage from his presence

title: Romans 8:28
summary: God works for the good of his people, including conformity to Christ.
context: The surrounding passage speaks of groaning, weakness, and the Spirit’s intercession. Verse 29 identifies conformity to Christ as God’s purpose.
distinction: God can work through genuine losses for the ultimate good of his people.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Romans 8
insights.quote: though God does not immediately succour his people, he yet does not forsake them

title: Prayer
context: In the Sermon on the Mount Jesus contrasts prayer to the Father with prayer performed for an audience.
distinction: Let the Father’s name and kingdom order requests for daily bread, pardon, and protection.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Matthew 6
insights.quote: if they wish to pray in a right manner, to enter into their closet

title: Repentance
context: Paul describes how the Corinthians responded to his painful letter by taking their wrongdoing seriously.
distinction: Godly grief moves toward repentance. Evaluate sorrow by the response it produces.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · 2 Corinthians 7
insights.quote: a sorrow for sin, because it was committed against a God of infinite holiness, justice, and truth, goodness, grace, and mercy

title: Faith
context: Hebrews urges a pressured congregation to persevere and then recalls believers who relied on God’s promises.
distinction: Trust God’s character even when the outcome remains unseen.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Hebrews 11
insights.quote: faith can be no more separated from patience than from itself

title: Grace
context: The appearance of grace teaches believers how to live as they await Christ’s appearing.
distinction: Grace pardons sinners and trains them in holiness.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Titus 2
insights.quote: instructs in real piety, and constrains to obedience to the will of God

title: Hope
context: Peter writes to scattered believers facing trials and identifies Jesus’ resurrection as the ground of their hope.
distinction: Anchor hope in the inheritance God keeps and in the risen Christ.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · 1 Peter 1
insights.quote: the resurrection of Christ is what is the means of, and lays a solid foundation of hope

title: Love of Neighbor
context: A lawyer asks whom he must count as a neighbor. Jesus describes a Samaritan who crosses social boundaries to help a wounded man.
distinction: Show mercy to the person in need, including across divisions.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Luke 10
insights.quote: such like acts of beneficence and kindness, though to a person of a different nation and religion, and though even an enemy

title: Humility
context: Paul appeals for unity and presents Christ’s self-emptying path of servanthood and obedience.
distinction: Use status and ability for others’ good as you follow Christ’s example.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Philippians 2
insights.quote: This grace of humility is an excellent ornament to a Christian, and wonderfully useful in Christian societies.

title: Wisdom
context: James places the prayer for wisdom in a discussion of trials and endurance.
distinction: Ask God for wisdom to act faithfully under pressure.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · James 1
insights.quote: it intends wisdom to behave aright under temptations or afflictions

title: Temptation
context: Paul recalls Israel’s failures as warnings to a church tempted by idolatry.
distinction: Take temptation seriously, trust God’s faithfulness, and act on the escape he provides.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · 1 Corinthians 10
insights.quote: they are a lesson to us, that we may not provoke the anger of God as they did

title: Anger
context: James links listening, restraint in speech, and putting away wickedness to receiving God’s word.
distinction: Slow your response and test anger against the righteousness God desires.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · James 1
insights.quote: wholesome advice, good instructions, and the gracious experiences of the saints

title: Speech
context: James begins by warning teachers, then shows how a small tongue can direct or damage a whole community.
distinction: Let the dignity of people made in God’s likeness govern how you speak about them.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · James 3
insights.quote: he proceeds to consider the evidence of a religious man, suggested in James 1:26 who is one that bridles the tongue

title: Work
context: Paul addresses enslaved people within a Roman household code and reminds them that Christ sees their labor and promises an inheritance.
distinction: Work with integrity before Christ, and read this alongside the duty of justice in 4:1.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Colossians 3
insights.quote: they appear to concern servants only, and what they do under that character, and under the discharge of their duty

title: Rest & Sabbath
context: The Pharisees challenge the disciples for plucking grain on the Sabbath, and Jesus appeals to David’s need.
distinction: Honor the purpose of God’s gift of rest under the authority of the Lord of the Sabbath.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Mark 2
insights.quote: he might have an opportunity of attending divine worship, both in public and private

title: Generosity
context: Paul is organizing a collection for believers in need and asks the Corinthians to give willingly.
distinction: Give cheerfully according to your means and use God’s provision to meet others’ needs.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · 2 Corinthians 9
insights.quote: He now commends alms-giving by a beautiful similitude, comparing it to sowing

title: Contentment
context: Paul pairs godliness with contentment as he corrects teachers who turn religion into a means of gain.
distinction: Receive ordinary provision gratefully and resist measuring spiritual health by wealth.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · 1 Timothy 6
insights.quote: as it shows itself in outward worship, and in all acts of holiness

title: Hospitality
context: Paul describes how genuine love becomes visible in the life of the church.
distinction: Share resources with believers in need and actively make room for guests.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Romans 12
insights.quote: all disguises are to be cast aside, and that love is to arise from pure sincerity of mind

title: Church Unity
context: After describing God’s saving work, Paul appeals for a way of life consistent with their calling.
distinction: Maintain Spirit-given unity through patience, humility, and shared allegiance to one Lord.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Ephesians 4
insights.quote: supposes that this union does already exist

title: Spiritual Gifts
context: Paul traces diverse gifts to the same Spirit and says their purpose is the common good.
distinction: Use gifts to serve the church. The Spirit decides how to distribute them.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · 1 Corinthians 12
insights.quote: it is befitting that there should be a distinction of gifts as well as of offices, and yet all harmonize in one

title: Baptism
context: Paul appeals to baptism while answering whether grace gives permission to continue in sin.
distinction: Baptism points to Christ’s death and resurrection and calls the baptized to walk in new life. Christians differ on subjects and mode.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Romans 6
insights.quote: they who imagine that gratuitous righteousness is given us by him, apart from newness of life, shamefully rend Christ asunder

title: Lord’s Supper
context: The Corinthians’ divisions and unequal meals prompt Paul to recall the Lord’s institution of the Supper.
distinction: The Supper proclaims Christ’s death and calls the church to self-examination and regard for fellow believers.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · 1 Corinthians 11
insights.quote: a remembrance of Christ, and a declaration of his sufferings and death

title: Resurrection
context: Paul reasons from Christ’s resurrection to the future of believers, drawing a contrast between Adam and Christ.
distinction: Christian hope depends on Christ’s bodily resurrection and looks to the resurrection of his people.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · 1 Corinthians 15
insights.quote: He now begins to prove the resurrection of all of us from that of Christ

title: Trinity
context: The risen Jesus commands disciples to baptize in the singular name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
distinction: The church confesses one God and distinguishes the Father, Son, and Spirit named together here.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Matthew 28
insights.quote: by the authority of these three divine persons

title: Deity of Christ
context: John opens with language recalling Genesis, presenting the Word as already present when creation began.
distinction: The Word who becomes flesh in verse 14 is distinct from the Father and fully divine.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · John 1
insights.quote: In this introduction he asserts the eternal Divinity of Christ

title: Holy Spirit
context: On the eve of his death, Jesus promises disciples another Advocate who will remain with them.
distinction: Receive the Spirit as God’s abiding presence with Christ’s people.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · John 14
insights.quote: by opening and applying the precious promises of the Gospel to them

title: Assurance
context: John explains why he writes to people already believing in the Son.
distinction: Assurance rests in God’s testimony that eternal life is in his Son.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · 1 John 5
insights.quote: The sum and substance of it, with respect to the person of Christ, and the security of salvation in him

title: Sanctification
context: Paul applies the call to please God to sexual conduct and regard for others.
distinction: Grow in holiness in embodied, everyday choices with the help of the Spirit God gives.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · 1 Thessalonians 4
insights.quote: External sanctification arises from this, and lies in holiness of life and conversation

title: Adoption
context: Paul contrasts fear in slavery with the family status of those led by the Spirit.
distinction: Believers approach God as Father and share Christ’s inheritance as they follow him through suffering.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Romans 8
insights.quote: by this mark God acknowledges them as his own people

title: Justification
context: After charging Jew and Gentile alike with sin, Paul explains how God displays his righteousness through Christ.
distinction: God justifies believers freely on account of Christ’s redeeming work.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Romans 3
insights.quote: which God communicates to man, and accepts alone, and owns as righteousness

title: Election
context: Paul blesses God for choosing and adopting his people in Christ, placing election in a prayer of praise.
distinction: God’s initiative leads to gratitude and holiness. Christian traditions differ on how election relates to human response.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Ephesians 1
insights.quote: The lofty terms in which he extolls the grace of God toward the Ephesians, are intended to rouse their hearts to gratitude

title: Providence
context: After Jacob dies, Joseph’s brothers fear retaliation for selling him. Joseph names both their evil intent and God’s saving purpose.
distinction: God can accomplish good through events that involve real wrongdoing. Joseph responds with provision and mercy.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Genesis 50
insights.quote: he designed good should come by it, and he brought good out of it

title: Lament
context: The psalm moves from repeated questions to petition and ultimately to confidence in God’s steadfast love.
distinction: Faith can name the distress honestly, ask for help, and cling to God’s character.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Psalm 13
insights.quote: by faith we apprehend his invisible providence

title: Peacemaking
context: Jesus blesses peacemakers among the Beatitudes that describe life in his kingdom.
distinction: Actively seek reconciliation in ways that reflect God’s character.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Matthew 5
insights.quote: labor to settle differences among others

title: Love of Enemies
context: Jesus points to the Father who sends sun and rain on the righteous and unrighteous alike.
distinction: Pray for opponents and extend practical goodwill without waiting for reciprocity.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Matthew 5
insights.quote: his person be loved, tenderness be used to him, and pity shown him

title: Justice & Mercy
context: In a covenant dispute, extravagant proposed sacrifices lead to a reminder of the life God requires.
distinction: Practice justice, love mercy, and walk humbly with God in ordinary decisions.

insights.author: Matthew Henry
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Micah 6
insights.quote: we must delight in it, as our God does, must be glad of an opportunity to do good, and do it cheerfully

title: Parents & Children
context: Paul addresses children and fathers in turn, giving duties to both within the household.
distinction: Children honor parents, and parents exercise authority through patient, Christ-centered nurture.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Ephesians 6
insights.quote: Obedience is the evidence of that honor which children owe to their parents

title: Singleness
context: Paul weighs marriage and singleness against present distress and the advantage of undivided devotion.
distinction: Recognize singleness as a real opportunity to serve the Lord, while honoring the freedom to marry.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · 1 Corinthians 7
insights.quote: they might be more free from the cares and encumbrances of life, and more at liberty to serve the Lord

title: Sexual Integrity
context: Paul grounds bodily conduct in union with Christ, future resurrection, and the Spirit’s presence.
distinction: Honor God with the body because it belongs to Christ.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · 1 Corinthians 6
insights.quote: which lays her under the greatest obligation to preserve an inviolable chastity to him, and to love and honour him

title: Civil Authority
context: After forbidding personal vengeance in chapter 12, Paul explains the public responsibilities of rulers and subjects.
distinction: Respect rightful authority and meet civil obligations, with loyalty to God remaining supreme (Acts 5:29).

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Romans 13
insights.quote: such duties as were relative to them as members of a civil society

title: Grief
context: Paul comforts believers worried that Christians who died might miss the Lord’s return.
distinction: Grieve with the hope that the risen Jesus will gather his people, including those who have died.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · 1 Thessalonians 4
insights.quote: Let, therefore, the grief of the pious be mixed with consolation, which may train them to patience.

title: Creation & Stewardship
context: God places the human in the garden and gives him the work of cultivating and keeping it.
distinction: Treat care for creation as part of responsible human work under God.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Genesis 2
insights.quote: let every one regard himself as the steward of God in all things which he possesses

title: Evangelism
context: Jesus redirects the disciples from calculating the kingdom’s timing to bearing Spirit-empowered witness.
distinction: Bear witness to Christ across geographic and social boundaries.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Acts 1
insights.quote: their business was to testify of the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that followed

title: Fasting
context: Jesus addresses fasting alongside giving and praying, warning against piety performed for public praise.
distinction: When you fast, direct the practice to God and keep it free of display.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Matthew 6
insights.quote: to have God as the witness of their actions

title: Genesis 1:26
context: The plural deliberation is followed by singular narration in verse 27. The passage identifies humanity, male and female, as God’s image.
distinction: The immediate emphasis is human dignity and vocation. Christians may read the plural in light of later revelation while recognizing other proposed explanations.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Genesis 1
insights.quote: when he approaches the most excellent of all his works, he enters into consultation

title: Genesis 3:15
context: God’s judgment on the serpent announces lasting conflict between the serpent and the woman’s offspring.
distinction: Christians see an early anticipation of victory over evil fulfilled in Christ. The immediate oracle speaks in the language of offspring and conflict.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Genesis 3
insights.quote: the whole Church of God, under its Head, will gloriously exult over him

title: Genesis 22:2
context: The narrator calls the command a test. God stops Abraham and provides a ram in Isaac’s place.
distinction: Read the event as a unique test of Abraham’s trust in God’s promise, ending with God’s provision.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Genesis 22
insights.quote: whatever favor he could hope for from God, was included in this single promise

title: Exodus 9:12
context: The plague narrative also describes Pharaoh hardening his own heart (8:15, 32). Here God hardens Pharaoh as foretold.
distinction: Hold together God’s sovereign judgment and Pharaoh’s culpable refusal. The text affirms both.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Exodus 9
insights.quote: He having often, and so long hardened his own heart, God gave him up to judicial hardness of heart

title: Exodus 20:5
context: The warning about generations occurs in the prohibition of idolatry and stands alongside much wider covenant mercy.
distinction: Idolatry has generational consequences. Ezekiel 18:20 also affirms that each person answers for his own sin.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Exodus 20
insights.quote: meaning chiefly, if not solely, the iniquity of idolatry

title: Leviticus 19:28
context: These commands address Israel’s holiness, placing marks for the dead alongside practices surrounding mourning and divination.
distinction: Read the prohibition within Israel’s covenant and consider the practice’s purpose and associations when applying its principle today.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Leviticus 19
insights.quote: there were who marked their bodies with a known figure, by burning, for the dead

title: Deuteronomy 6:4
context: Israel’s confession of the one LORD introduces the command to love him wholly and teach his words at home.
distinction: The confession demands exclusive allegiance to the LORD and grounds daily instruction in his word.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Deuteronomy 6
insights.quote: unless they abode in the One God, who had laid them under such obligations to Himself

title: Joshua 1:9
context: God commissions Joshua to lead Israel after Moses and ties courage to obedience to the law.
distinction: Take courage in following God faithfully. The conquest commission belongs to Joshua’s historical task.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Joshua 1
insights.quote: the Lord, by bringing his own authority distinctly forward, relieves his servant from care and hesitancy

title: Judges 6:36–40
context: Gideon asks for two signs after receiving a clear commission and seeing God’s earlier sign.
distinction: God’s patience with Gideon encourages fearful people. The story records his hesitation and God’s accommodation.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Judges 6
insights.quote: was willing to have a confirmation of his faith

title: 1 Samuel 16:7
context: Samuel assumes Eliab’s appearance makes him the right king. God chooses David from among Jesse’s sons.
distinction: Recognize the limits of outward assessment. God sees character and purposes beyond what viewers can judge.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · 1 Samuel 16
insights.quote: the inward qualifications and endowments of the mind are seen by the Lord

title: 2 Chronicles 7:14
context: God answers Solomon after the temple dedication, naming drought and other covenant judgments upon Israel.
distinction: The promise concerns Israel, the temple, and its land. Its call to humble prayer and repentance has enduring relevance.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · 2 Chronicles 7
insights.quote: when the people of Israel should humble themselves in prayer and supplication, the Lord would be attentive to them, and forgive them

title: Job 1:21
context: Job tears his robe and mourns before worshiping God in response to terrible loss.
distinction: Grief and worship can coexist. Job’s response acknowledges dependence on God amid unexplained loss.

insights.author: Matthew Henry
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Job 1
insights.quote: Death strips us of all our enjoyments; clothing can neither warm nor adorn a dead body.

title: Psalm 37:4
context: The psalm counsels the righteous against envy when wrongdoers prosper, urging trust and patient waiting.
distinction: Delight in God within the psalm’s pattern of entrusting your way to him.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Psalm 37
insights.quote: the vain and fickle joys with which the world is deluded, and the true repose enjoyed by the godly

title: Psalm 46:10
context: The psalm calls readers to see God end wars and declare his supremacy among the nations.
distinction: The call to be still summons surrender before God’s rule. It also comforts those who take refuge in him.

insights.author: Matthew Henry
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Psalm 46
insights.quote: Let his enemies be still, and threaten no more

title: Psalm 51:5
context: David confesses particular sins and also describes the depth of his corruption from the beginning of life.
distinction: Confession goes deeper than isolated acts. David appeals to divine mercy for his whole condition.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Psalm 51
insights.quote: it is beside his scope and design to expose the sins of others, much less his own parents

title: Psalm 82:6
context: God rebukes unjust figures called gods and announces that they will die like men. Their identity is debated.
distinction: The psalm centers on God’s judgment of unjust rule. Jesus invokes its wording in John 10:34–36 during his defense.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Psalm 82
insights.quote: he constituted them judges and magistrates, invested them with such an office, by which they came to have this title

title: Psalm 137:9
context: An exile remembers Jerusalem’s destruction and voices a horrifying reversal against Babylon.
distinction: Read the cry in the setting of trauma and divine judgment. Romans 12:19 entrusts vengeance to God.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Psalm 137
insights.quote: Nor is this desired from a spirit of revenge, but for the glory of divine justice

title: Proverbs 22:6
context: The saying is part of a collection of short wisdom observations about patterns in life. Its expression about the child’s way is debated.
distinction: Take formative training seriously and read this as wisdom about a pattern in life.

insights.author: Matthew Henry
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Proverbs 22
insights.quote: But early training may be a means of their recovering themselves

title: Ecclesiastes 3:1
context: The poem names contrasting seasons before reflecting on human inability to grasp God’s work from beginning to end.
distinction: Attend to the season you are in with humility about your control over events.

insights.author: Matthew Henry
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Ecclesiastes 3
insights.quote: providence calls to weep and mourn

title: Isaiah 7:14
context: The sign is given to Ahaz amid the Syro-Ephraimite crisis, with an approaching change before the child matures.
distinction: Read the sign in Ahaz’s crisis and in Matthew 1:22–23, where Jesus’ birth fulfills Immanuel in its climactic sense.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Isaiah 7
insights.quote: Ahaz had already refused the sign which the Lord offered to him

title: Isaiah 53:5
context: The servant bears the sorrows and iniquities of others, with healing tied to their straying and guilt.
distinction: The servant secures restoration by bearing sin. Matthew 8:17 also connects the servant to Jesus’ healing ministry.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Isaiah 53
insights.quote: by his death our sins have been expiated, and salvation has been obtained for us

title: Ezekiel 18:20
context: Ezekiel answers the exiles’ complaint about inherited guilt by contrasting the conduct of parents and children.
distinction: God calls each person to repent and answers each for their conduct. Harm can still reach across generations.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Ezekiel 18
insights.quote: God is a just judge and treats every one according to his conduct

title: Malachi 3:10
context: God addresses Israel’s withholding of tithes that supplied the temple storehouse and promises covenant blessings in the land.
distinction: Take worship and material faithfulness seriously, and read the provision promised here within Israel’s covenant.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Malachi 3
insights.quote: there were places in the temple where the tithe was put, and from thence distributed to the priests and Levites

title: Matthew 5:17
context: Jesus states his relation to the Law and Prophets before showing the depth of kingdom righteousness in the rest of the chapter.
distinction: Read the Scriptures through Jesus’ fulfillment and hear his call for righteousness that reaches the heart.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Matthew 5
insights.quote: what had hitherto appeared only in figures

title: Matthew 5:29
context: The eye and hand sayings follow Jesus’ diagnosis of lust as a matter of the heart.
distinction: The severe imagery calls for decisive removal of occasions for sin. The heart remains the target.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Matthew 5
insights.quote: the justice of God ought to stand higher in our estimation

title: Matthew 7:7
context: Jesus compares God’s hearing of prayer to a father giving good things to children.
distinction: Ask confidently with trust in the Father’s goodness and judgment about what to give.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Matthew 7
insights.quote: asking of God in prayer, for such things as are wanting

title: Matthew 12:31–32
context: Jesus responds after opponents attribute a Spirit-empowered deliverance to the ruler of demons.
distinction: The warning concerns a grave rejection of the Spirit’s testimony to Jesus. Its setting helps distinguish it from anxious intrusive thoughts.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Matthew 12
insights.quote: knowingly and willingly to pour contempt on the Spirit of God

title: Matthew 16:18
context: Jesus speaks after Peter confesses him as the Christ, the Son of the living God.
distinction: Christ builds and preserves his church. Traditions differ over how Peter, his confession, and later church authority relate to the rock.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Matthew 16
insights.quote: Christ declares how highly he is delighted with the confession of Peter

title: Matthew 19:24
context: A rich man walks away grieving. The disciples are astonished when Jesus describes the difficulty of a rich person entering the kingdom.
distinction: Receive salvation as something God makes possible. Wealth can expose rival allegiance.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Matthew 19
insights.quote: it is proper that they should perceive how difficult it is to ascend

title: Matthew 24:34
context: Jesus speaks of tribulation and his coming in a discourse prompted by questions about the temple and the end.
distinction: Take seriously both the assurance of fulfillment and the unknown day and hour. Interpretations differ over the scope of “this generation.”

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Matthew 24
insights.quote: within fifty years the city was destroyed and the temple was razed

title: Mark 16:16
context: The commission pairs faith and baptism, and explicitly names unbelief in the condemnation clause. These verses belong to the disputed longer ending.
distinction: Distinguish the ordinary summons to believe and be baptized from the textual question about Mark 16:9–20.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Mark 16
insights.quote: who comes to him as a poor perishing sinner, and ventures on him, and commits himself to him, and lives upon him

title: Luke 14:26
context: Jesus addresses crowds about counting the cost. Family and even one’s own life appear among competing attachments.
distinction: Give Jesus supreme allegiance, which can prove costly even in your closest relationships.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Luke 14
insights.quote: these are not to be preferred to Christ, or loved more than he

title: Luke 23:43
context: The dying criminal appeals to Jesus as king and receives a promise of being with him in Paradise.
distinction: The promise emphasizes immediate hope and fellowship with Jesus for a man unable to establish a record of good works.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Luke 23
insights.quote: promised him more than he asked for, and sooner than he expected

title: John 3:5
context: Jesus tells a teacher of Israel that entering the kingdom requires birth from above. Ezekiel 36:25–27 connects cleansing with God’s Spirit.
distinction: New birth comes from God’s Spirit and involves cleansing. Christians differ on whether water directly refers to baptism here.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · John 3
insights.quote: the Spirit of God is the only Author of a pure and upright nature

title: John 6:53
context: The bread discourse repeatedly connects eternal life to believing in Jesus and speaks of his flesh given for the life of the world.
distinction: Depend on Jesus and his life-giving death. Christians differ on the relationship between this language and the Eucharist.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · John 6
insights.quote: the way by which he becomes one with us, is, when our faith relies on his death

title: John 10:30
context: Jesus’ statement follows his claim that his sheep are secure in both his hand and the Father’s hand.
distinction: Father and Son are distinct and act with one divine power to preserve the sheep.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · John 10
insights.quote: Christ is speaking of the impossibility of plucking any of the sheep, out of his own and his Father's hands

title: Acts 2:38
context: Peter calls his hearers to repent and be baptized after announcing the risen Jesus as Lord and Christ.
distinction: Baptism is the commanded public response to the gospel. Traditions differ on how baptism relates to forgiveness here.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · Acts 2
insights.quote: consider him, and believe in him, as the true Messiah and Saviour of the world

title: Romans 7:19
context: Paul describes a conflict involving desire, sin, and the law before crying out for rescue through Jesus Christ.
distinction: The passage exposes sin’s grip and directs readers to Christ. Interpreters differ on whose experience Paul portrays.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Romans 7
insights.quote: the faithful, however rightly they may be influenced, are yet so conscious of their own infirmity

title: Romans 9:13
context: Paul quotes Malachi’s account of Jacob and Esau as part of his argument that God’s word to Israel has held firm.
distinction: God’s saving purpose depends on his mercy and initiative. The argument uses individuals with covenant and national significance.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Romans 9
insights.quote: Jacob obtained this favor through the kindness of God, and not through his own merit

title: 1 Corinthians 6:9–10
context: Paul addresses a church embroiled in disputes, lists conduct at odds with God’s kingdom, and recalls their washing and justification.
distinction: Take the warning and promise together. Christ cleanses sinners and calls them to a changed life.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · 1 Corinthians 6
insights.quote: those who inflict injury on their brethren, who defraud or circumvent others

title: Galatians 3:28
context: Paul reasons from faith and baptism into Christ to equal status as heirs of Abraham’s promise.
distinction: Ethnic, social, and sexual distinctions confer no privileged claim to the inheritance. Other passages inform particular questions about church roles.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Galatians 3
insights.quote: Whatever may have been their former differences, Christ alone is able to unite them all.

title: Ephesians 5:22
context: The marriage instructions follow a call to submit to one another and culminate in an extended command for husbands to love as Christ did.
distinction: Read the instructions together under Christ’s authority. The pattern of husbandly love is self-sacrifice.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Ephesians 5
insights.quote: some are more closely bound to each other, according to their respective callings

title: 1 Timothy 2:12
context: The instructions sit within counsel for congregational conduct and appeal to creation. The meaning and scope of the authority language are debated.
distinction: Read the teaching together with Paul’s positive command that women learn. Churches differ on how the prohibition applies to teaching offices.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · 1 Timothy 2
insights.quote: Timothy, no doubt, received much advantage, from the private teachings and instructions of his mother Eunice

title: Hebrews 6:4–6
context: A sharp warning about falling away is followed by a field analogy and confidence in better things concerning the readers.
distinction: Take apostasy seriously and pursue persevering faith. Reformed and other readings differ on the prior spiritual state described.

insights.author: John Calvin
insights.source: Commentaries (Calvin Translation Society) · Hebrews 6
insights.quote: the Apostle does not without reason forewarn all the disciples of Christ to beware in time

title: James 2:24
context: James challenges someone who claims faith without works, using Abraham’s obedience and Rahab’s protection of the messengers.
distinction: Living faith acts. James tests an empty profession, and Paul in Romans 3 rejects reliance on works for justification.

insights.author: John Gill
insights.source: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments · James 2
insights.quote: Not as causes procuring his justification, but as effects declaring it
